info.title: Arcanist REST API
info.description: REST equivalent of the Arcanist GraphQL API (/graphql), without subscriptions. Authenticate with POST /rest/v1/auth/login and send the access token as a Bearer token.

get.summary: Whether ffmpeg can be downloaded for this machine, and how its download goes.

post.summary: Downloads ffmpeg (a static build from BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds, checked against its SHA-256) into the data folder.
Creates a folder on the server, to pick it as a library location.

get.summary: Checks the ffmpeg at the given path, or which one would be found automatically.

post.summary: Reads an mStream installation, from its folder on this server or from its server, to choose what to import.

get.summary: Looks for DLNA/UPnP media servers on the local networks, to copy music from once set up.
The media server at a description URL.
A folder of a media server; 0 is the root.
Looks for other Arcanist servers on the local networks, to bring one over.

post.summary: What another Arcanist holds, read with its migration code (or its P2P migration link), to choose what to bring.
The backups in a folder of this server or an S3 bucket that carry a server, to restore it instead of setting it up.
Whether the password opens a snapshot's server data.
Restores the server from a snapshot (its database, settings and keys) and restarts to install it; afterwards, if asked, the libraries' missing files come back too.

get.summary: Public description of the server. Does not require authentication.

The terms and conditions and the disclaimer, in a language, for this server (self-hosted, or part of LinkFast's service): the setup wizard asks administrators to accept them, and players their users (audience USER). Does not require authentication.

delete.summary: Removes a location and its tracks from the catalog; files on disk are not touched. A local library's only folder cannot be removed (last_source): move it instead. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.

post.summary: Moves a local library's folder to another folder of the server in the background: copies every file, points the library at the new folder and, unless keepOriginals, deletes the old files. Nothing is overwritten. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

get.summary: Library folder moves since the server started, the latest first, with their progress. Administrators only.
Folders on the server, for choosing library locations. Lists the file system roots when path is omitted. Administrators only.

post.summary: Creates a folder on the server, to pick it as a location. Administrators only.
Queues a scan, or returns the one already queued or running for the library. A full scan re-reads every file. Requires RUN_SCANS.
Moves the files of a finished organizing run back where they were, in the background. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES and a recent authentication.

put.summary: Rates a track 1–5 for the user, or clears the rating with null. With the single-star rating mode only 5 is accepted.
Makes a track one of the user's StarTracks (rates it 5), or not (clears a 5). Works with both rating modes.

get.summary: The user's StarTracks (the star in single-star mode, five stars otherwise), most recently starred first, with each song's AcoustID.

post.summary: Adds songs to the user's StarTracks, by track or by AcoustID (as Ultimate Cloud names them), at most 1000. By AcoustID, one of the song's tracks, unless one already is.
Takes songs from the user's StarTracks, by track or by AcoustID (every track of the song), at most 1000.

get.summary: The user's tracks rated at least minRating (5 for StarTracks), most recently rated first. With the single-star rating mode, only StarTracks.

post.summary: Reports that the user listened to a track. The server decides whether it counts as a play (30 seconds, and half the track or four minutes) or a skip.
Brings ratings and play counts an app kept on its own (at most 1000 of each per call). Ratings only fill gaps; play counts keep the highest.

get.summary: The user's counted plays, newest first.
Listening over a `period` (WEEK, MONTH, YEAR, ALL): the user's own, or another user's with VIEW_ALL_STATS. timeZone is an IANA id (UTC by default) for days and months.
What the libraries hold and how the server is listened to over a `period` (WEEK, MONTH, YEAR, ALL), per user; with libraryId, of one library. Requires VIEW_ALL_STATS.
Each library the user sees at a glance: songs, albums, files, size and length, and with VIEW_ALL_STATS its plays and listeners of the last 30 days.

put.summary: Chooses how users rate tracks: STARS (one to five) or STAR (a single star, kept as five). Nothing is lost when switching. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

get.summary: The server's other active users, to invite as playlist collaborators.

Every upload into the server's libraries, by any user and from any client (the admin panel, Ultimate Desktop, web players, phones, extensions), newest first, with optional filters. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES (only libraries the caller can access, unless administrator).

post.summary: Adds an audio file as `uploadToLibrary` does: into `libraryId` when given, else the target of the user's wish `wishId` when it has one, else the user's own choice (`myUploadSettings`), else the server's default for uploads (`uploadSettings`); `upload_library_required` without one. Requires UPLOAD.

get.summary: The library uploads go to when they name none (and wishes with no target of their own), or none.

put.summary: Sets the library uploads go to when they name none; null leaves the choice to each upload. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.

get.summary: The library the user chose for their uploads that name none, and where such an upload goes now (their choice, else the server's default).

put.summary: Chooses the library the user's uploads go to when they name none (one they can upload to: libraryId not_found otherwise); null goes back to the server's default. For apps that use the whole server as one library.

get.summary: How much music each library the user can access holds (files, tracks, bytes) and the free space of its disk when known, with the totals and the free space where the user's uploads go.
The user's uploads, newest first: files sent into libraries (and whether each is in the catalog yet) and songs sent to their own Ultimate Cloud library.

delete.summary: Forgets the user's finished uploads (what is still on its way stays). Returns how many were forgotten.

post.summary: Sends songs of this server (at most 1000) to the user's own Ultimate Cloud library, in the background; their progress is in myUploads. Needs the DOWNLOAD permission, and for a library another server shares, its permission to download.

get.summary: A song's analysis for DJ software (AI extension): beat grid, sections, energy, voice, mix and scratch points… `include` picks blocks (beats, onsets, energy, vocals, sections, silences, cues, loudness, key, stats; all but stats by default). 202 with status PENDING and its position in line until it is ready.

post.summary: Puts a song first in line for its analysis (it is going to be played soon).

get.summary: Analyses of the songs the user sees, from the least to the most recently analyzed (at most 200 a page): keep a cache with updatedSince set to the last analyzedAt held.

A short piece of a song, decoded (AI extension): `start` and `duration` (at most 8) in seconds, as a WAV file of 16-bit stereo at 44.1 kHz (`format=pcm16`, the only one). For scratching or previewing a part without downloading the song. Authenticate like /stream (Bearer, or `st` of a streamUrl). 503 transcoding_unavailable without ffmpeg.

Listening statistics per song (plays, skips and where, completions, how much is listened to, hours of the day): the user's, or the server's (everyone's together). From the least to the most recently played.
What the AI extension's analysis is doing, its progress and settings. Administrators only.

put.summary: Changes the AI extension's settings. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

post.summary: Analyzes every song again; the current analyses are served (as stale) until each is redone. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

get.summary: Artists, albums, tracks and playlists matching every word of the query (as word starts, ignoring accents and case), best first. first is per kind: 10 by default, at most 50.
The user's home page: recently played and added albums, mixes, most played, starred tracks, albums to rediscover or never played, and playlists. Empty sections are left out.
Mixes made for the user from their favorite artists, genres and decades, their favorites and music they never played. They change once a day.
A mix's tracks in play order. Besides the ids from mixes, any artist:<id>, genre:<id>, decade:<year> or track:<id> (a radio started from a track) works, ids without dashes.
Everything an artist page shows: top tracks, albums, albums the artist appears on, related artists and the artist's mix.

Pages of the running extensions the user may open from a player, in a window (an iframe) or a tab of its own, named in `language` (or Accept-Language). They get the session and the player's theme with the host protocol of docs/developers/extensions.md.
Whether the caller's StarTracks are shown to the devices of the local network (DLNA), and whether DLNA is on.

put.summary: Shows (true) or stops showing (false) the caller's StarTracks to the devices of the local network, as a folder of DLNA's StarTracks: only songs of the published libraries, to anyone there without signing in.

get.summary: Whether the server is in maintenance (migrating its database) and how far it got. Anyone can ask, also during maintenance.

put.summary: Uploads, downloads or both between a library and the Ultimate Cloud account (Cloud plan); nothing is deleted on either side. Administrators only; turning it on needs a recent authentication.

post.summary: Syncs a library with Ultimate Cloud now (otherwise every 6 hours). Administrators only.

get.summary: How much space Arcanist takes, part by part (the database too), its database's tables, how much is in the catalog and the music of each library. Measured at most every five minutes unless refresh is true. Administrators only.

How many songs have lyrics, how many of them are timed (and how many timed on this server), how many plain lyrics could be timed here, and whether the official extension that does it (Lyrics Sync) is installed and running. Administrators only.
No telemetry, and which outside services the server may use. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

put.summary: Chooses no telemetry (anonymous statistics off; linked accounts start without sending plays) and which outside services may be used: ALL, ULTIMATE_CLOUD_ONLY (no online services) or NONE (Ultimate Cloud's extension off too). What they leave out is turned off. The music server's own services are not affected. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

get.summary: The 100% open source mode, the server's edition and the closed source components installed. Administrators only.

put.summary: Turns the 100% open source mode on or off: while on, closed source extensions, players and tools are neither installed nor run (closed_source_disabled). Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

get.summary: Whether anonymous play counts go to Ultimate Cloud's global statistics. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

put.summary: Sends anonymous play counts to Ultimate Cloud's global statistics, or stops. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

get.summary: Audio of a track. Authenticate with a Bearer token or the `st` parameter of a track's streamUrl. `fileId` picks a specific copy; `download=true` sends the original as an attachment and requires DOWNLOAD. Without `format`, `maxBitRate` or `timeOffset` the original is sent with HTTP range support. `format` (see serverInfo.transcodingFormats) converts it, at `maxBitRate` kbit/s if given; `maxBitRate` alone converts to MP3 only when the original exceeds it. Converted audio has no range support: seek by requesting again with `timeOffset` in seconds. `client` (DESKTOP, WEB or MOBILE: an Ultimate client) applies that client's default quality (streamingDefaults) when the request asks for none. 503 transcoding_unavailable without ffmpeg.

head.summary: Audio of a track. Authenticate with a Bearer token or the `st` parameter of a track's streamUrl. `fileId` picks a specific copy; `download=true` sends the original as an attachment and requires DOWNLOAD. Without `format`, `maxBitRate` or `timeOffset` the original is sent with HTTP range support. `format` (see serverInfo.transcodingFormats) converts it, at `maxBitRate` kbit/s if given; `maxBitRate` alone converts to MP3 only when the original exceeds it. Converted audio has no range support: seek by requesting again with `timeOffset` in seconds. `client` (DESKTOP, WEB or MOBILE: an Ultimate client) applies that client's default quality (streamingDefaults) when the request asks for none. 503 transcoding_unavailable without ffmpeg.

get.summary: An album or track image by artworkId. `size` scales it so its longest side fits (64, 128, 256, 512 or 1024). Public and cacheable forever, so it can be used directly in image elements.
The user's choice of whose audio plays with music videos, and the one in effect.

put.summary: Chooses whose audio plays with music videos for the user (TRACK, VIDEO, or null for the server's default).

post.summary: Adds a track's music video (MP4, MKV, WebM, MOV) next to its copy in a library the user uploads to, named like it: the next scan links it and the server aligns it. Requires UPLOAD.

get.summary: A user's own copy of the music they can play (a local backup, without being an administrator): the original files, page by page, with library, path, size, audio hash and a resumable download URL. Requires DOWNLOAD.
The user's own data (ratings, StarTracks, play counts, plays, playlists) in the backups' format (docs/backups.md): `{ catalog, userData }`.
The signed-in user.
Devices where the signed-in user is currently signed in.

delete.summary: Signs out one of the signed-in user's devices.

post.summary: Changes the signed-in user's password and signs out their other devices.

get.summary: All users. Requires the MANAGE_USERS permission.

post.summary: Requires MANAGE_USERS and a recent authentication.

get.summary: A user by id. Requires the MANAGE_USERS permission.

put.summary: Requires MANAGE_USERS and a recent authentication.

delete.summary: Requires MANAGE_USERS and a recent authentication.

put.summary: Replaces the libraries explicitly granted to a user. Requires MANAGE_USERS and a recent authentication.

post.summary: Sets a new password and signs the user out everywhere. Requires MANAGE_USERS and a recent authentication.

get.summary: Libraries the signed-in user can access. With `includeVirtual`, first "All" (`virtual`), every one of them at once, named in `language` (or Accept-Language).

post.summary: Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.

get.summary: A library by id. Libraries the user cannot access are reported as not found.

put.summary: Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.

delete.summary: Removes the library and its tracks from the catalog; files on disk are not touched. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES and a recent authentication.

post.summary: Adds an audio file (the request body, `application/octet-stream`; its name in `fileName`) to a library the user can access, placed with the library's template and never overwriting. 201 when it entered the library (catalogued by a scan shortly after the last upload), 200 when the library already had that audio. `client` (PANEL, DESKTOP, WEB or MOBILE) says what sends it, for the log of uploads administrators see. Every upload goes through here (extensions too, in the server). Requires UPLOAD.
Checks that an S3 bucket answers with those keys, and how much music it holds. Needs the Cloud plan. Administrators only.
A library in an S3 bucket (any S3-compatible service). Needs the Cloud plan. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

put.summary: Renames a library (only its name). Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES, or to own it (a personal library). duplicate when another library has that name.

post.summary: Adds a location to a library. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.

get.summary: Most recent scans first, of one library or of all libraries the user can see. Requires RUN_SCANS or MANAGE_LIBRARIES.
A scan by id, including live progress while it runs. Poll it to follow a scan. Requires RUN_SCANS or MANAGE_LIBRARIES.

post.summary: Requires RUN_SCANS.

get.summary: Progress of the background audio analysis (loudness, fingerprints, waveforms, tempo and key). Poll it to follow progress. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.

put.summary: Turns the background audio analysis on or off. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

get.summary: Where Arcanist found ffmpeg, and the progress of a download. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

put.summary: Uses the ffmpeg at the given path, or finds one automatically when null. Fails with not_ffmpeg if it does not work. Administrators only, with a recent password.

post.summary: Downloads ffmpeg (a static GPL build from BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds) into the data directory in the background. Poll the status to follow it. Administrators only, with a recent password.

delete.summary: Deletes the ffmpeg Arcanist downloaded; the next one found (the configured one, the system's) takes its place. Administrators only, with a recent password.

get.summary: The conversion cache and the versions of the music made ahead of time (passive transcoding), with their progress. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

put.summary: The conversion cache (on or off, size, age) and the versions to make ahead of time, of which libraries. Versions nobody asks for any more are removed. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

delete.summary: Empties the conversion cache; the versions made ahead of time stay. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

get.summary: The quality each kind of Ultimate client (desktop, web, mobile) plays by default. The stream applies it to requests with `client` and no quality of their own; clients show it as their default.

put.summary: Sets the quality each kind of Ultimate client plays by default: the original (no format; with maxBitRate, MP3 only above it) or a format and bit rate. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

get.summary: Pairs of tracks whose audio is similar but not enough to merge them automatically, most similar first. `status` is OPEN (default) or DISMISSED. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.

post.summary: Merges an open pair into keepTrackId, one of its two tracks, and returns it. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.
Keeps the two tracks of an open pair apart; it is not proposed again. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.

put.summary: Sets the library's path template and whether files added to it are organized automatically. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.

get.summary: What organizing the library would move, with the given template or the library's own. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.

post.summary: Moves the library's files to the paths its template gives them, in the background. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES and a recent authentication.

get.summary: The library's latest organizing runs, newest first. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.
Folders whose files are imported into libraries. Administrators only.

post.summary: Administrators only.

put.summary: Administrators only.

delete.summary: Stops importing from the folder and forgets its history; its files are not touched. Administrators only.

get.summary: Files found in drop folders, most recently changed first: in the given `status`, or else those still in a drop folder. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.
How many files of the drop folders are in each state. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.

post.summary: Imports a file even though it is incomplete or a duplicate (then as another copy of its track), first writing the given tags into it. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.
Looks at a file again, as if it had just been dropped. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.
Leaves a file in its drop folder; it is looked at again only if it changes. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.
Moves a file to its drop folder's trash, from which it is deleted after a while. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES.

get.summary: The user's playlists, those they collaborate on and public ones, most recently changed first. With `changedSince`, only those changed after it (deleted ones are not listed: the whole list says which are left).
A playlist by id. Playlists the user cannot see are reported as not found.

put.summary: Renames, describes and shares a playlist. Owner only.

delete.summary: Owner only.

get.summary: A playlist's tracks in order, page by page (100 by default, at most 1000).

post.summary: Adds tracks at the end or at a position. Owner and collaborators.
Makes a private playlist of the user's own with the tracks of one they can see.
Removes entries. Owner and collaborators.
Moves entries together to a position, keeping their order. Owner and collaborators.

put.summary: Replaces the users who can add, remove and reorder the playlist's tracks. Owner only.

get.summary: The user's wish list: songs they want (newest first), then those that arrived (by when). Optionally only the WANTED or the OBTAINED ones. With scope=ALL, everyone's wishes, each with its owner (requires VIEW_ALL_WISHES).

post.summary: Adds a song to the user's wish list (title and artist; album, duration, MusicBrainz recording or AcoustID narrow it). When a library the user can play has it already, it comes obtained (foundWhenAdded).

Reads a song's link from a streaming service (Spotify, YouTube Music, Deezer, Apple Music, MusicBrainz, Tidal, SoundCloud, Bandcamp…) to fill a wish: title, artist, album, duration, the MusicBrainz recording and a cover (kept in the artwork cache). Adds nothing: pass what it returns to AddWish with sourceUrl and artworkId. Needs external services allowed (external_services_disabled); wish_link_not_a_song for albums or playlists, wish_link_unreadable when the page does not say the song.

put.summary: Changes a wish of the user. Another song makes it wanted again, and it is looked for at once.

delete.summary: Removes a wish (wanted or obtained) from the user's list.

post.summary: The user saw the wishes that came true (WishListResult.unseen goes to 0). Returns how many were new.

get.summary: Installed web players; the default one is served at /. Administrators only.

post.summary: Installs (or updates) the web player in an uploaded .zip with arcanist-frontend.json at its root (form field `file`). Administrators only, with a recent authentication.
Downloads a web player's .zip and installs it (or updates it). It runs with the user's session: install only what you trust. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

get.summary: The web players of the catalog (github.com/linkfast/arcanist-extensions by default: Ultimate Web Player and those anyone publishes), named in `language`, with what is installed here. Read again after an hour, or now with `refresh`. Administrators only.

post.summary: Installs (or updates) a web player of the catalog, checked against the SHA-256 the catalog publishes, and serves it at / when `makeDefault`. It runs with its users' sessions. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

put.summary: Serves this web player at /. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

delete.summary: Removes an installed web player. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

get.summary: Built-in and installed extensions, with what happened to them at startup. Administrators only.

post.summary: Installs (or updates) the extension in an uploaded .zip with arcanist-extension.json at its root (form field `file`); it runs once enabled and the server restarts. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

get.summary: The extension catalog (github.com/linkfast/arcanist-extensions by default), named in `language`, with what is installed here. Read again after an hour, or now with `refresh`. Administrators only.

post.summary: Installs (or updates) an extension of the catalog, checked against the SHA-256 the catalog publishes, and switches it on unless `enable` is false; it runs after a restart. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

Downloads an extension's .zip and installs it (or updates it); it runs once enabled and the server restarts. Extensions run inside the server with full trust. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

get.summary: An installed extension's settings page, as it describes it (sections with fields, statuses and actions), for the admin panel to draw. Administrators only.

put.summary: Saves the fields of an extension's settings page. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

post.summary: Runs an action of an extension's settings page, with its fields' values. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

put.summary: Switches an extension on or off. Built-in extensions and switching off apply at once; an installed one runs after a restart. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

delete.summary: Removes an installed extension (it stops at once and is gone after a restart). Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

get.summary: The user's app passwords, for Subsonic and mStream apps; their secrets are never shown again.

post.summary: Creates a password for one app (Subsonic, mStream) and returns its secret, only this once. Needs a recent authentication.

delete.summary: Revokes one of the user's app passwords.

get.summary: The latest imports from mStream, newest first. Administrators only.

post.summary: Imports from mStream: the chosen libraries, its users (who keep their passwords) and their playlists, ratings and play counts, which arrive once the new libraries are scanned (or, from a server, when each user first signs in). Needs a recent authentication.
Reads an mStream installation on this server (its folder or configuration file) without changing it: its libraries, users and their data. Administrators only.
Reads the libraries and users of an mStream server through its API, signing in with one of its administrators. Administrators only.

delete.summary: Removes a finished import from mStream from the history; what it brought stays. An import from an mStream server stays while some of its users have not signed in. Administrators only.

post.summary: Tries again the files of an import from an mStream server that could not be copied. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.
Clears the history of migrations from mStream and DLNA servers (only finished ones, and not the mStream imports still needed to sign in); returns how many went. Administrators only.

get.summary: The DLNA media server: whether it is on, what it publishes and the addresses devices find. Administrators only.

put.summary: Sets the name devices show, the libraries published on the local network (to anyone there, without signing in) and the folders of the tree. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.
Pauses (false) or resumes (true) counting the plays of "play to" in users' statistics; renderers keep playing. Administrators only.

get.summary: Devices on the local network Arcanist can play to (DLNA renderers); empty while DLNA is off.

post.summary: Adds a renderer by the URL of its UPnP description, for networks where it is not found by itself. Administrators only.

get.summary: What a renderer is doing: its state, position, volume and Arcanist's queue on it.

post.summary: Plays tracks on a renderer, in the best format it plays (lossless first). The plays count for the caller.
Plays, pauses, stops, skips or seeks on a renderer.

Changes the queue playing on a renderer: append or insert tracks after the one playing, remove, move or jump to an entry. The track playing goes on. Only who started the queue (or an administrator) while it plays.
Asks the local network for renderers now and returns the list a few seconds later.

put.summary: Sets a renderer's volume, 0–100.

get.summary: Server audio: whether it plays, on which device, and the server's audio devices. Administrators only. The server plays through "play to" as the renderer "server".

put.summary: Chooses the device server audio plays on (the system's default when null) and the name it shows. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

post.summary: Plays a short tone on the server's device, to check it; refused while a queue plays. Administrators only.

get.summary: How the mStream extension behaves with the mStream apps: the star threshold, signing in with the user's password and the apps' own functions. Administrators only.

put.summary: Changes how the mStream extension behaves with the mStream apps. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

post.summary: A new pairing code for the mStream apps' quick connect: apps that scanned the old one are disconnected. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

get.summary: The P2P network: whether it runs, this server's node id, its relay and what goes through it now. Administrators only.

put.summary: Turns the P2P network on or off and sets its relay, the name peers see and the global limits. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

get.summary: Nodes allowed through the P2P network, with their rules and traffic: the caller's devices, or every peer for administrators.

post.summary: An invitation to pair a device with the caller (or, for administrators, another user), valid 30 minutes. The app reads it (as a QR code) and pairs through the P2P network.
An invitation for another Arcanist server to receive libraries, with rules and an optional end, valid 7 days. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

put.summary: Changes a peer's name, rules, end and (for a server) shared libraries. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

post.summary: Ends a peer's access at once. Users revoke their own devices; administrators, any peer.

get.summary: Libraries other servers share with this one, each shown here as a library. Administrators only.

post.summary: Accepts another server's share with its invitation link: its libraries become one library here, scanned at once (nothing is downloaded: the music streams from that server). Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

Copies a received share's files into a folder of one of this server's libraries, when its owner allows downloads. Runs in the background; its progress shows in the share. Administrators only, with a recent authentication.

put.summary: Whether plays of a received share's music go to its server, with the users' names, when it counts them (its rule countPlays). Administrators only.

get.summary: How libraries other servers share are played here: their cache (and what it takes) and where their songs are converted. Administrators only.

put.summary: The cache of other servers' music (on or off, size, age) and where their songs are converted. Administrators only.

delete.summary: Empties the cache of other servers' music; it is fetched again as it is played. Administrators only.

get.summary: The P2P network's activity a page at a time (1 to 500), newest first, by peer, kind or words in the peer's name and the detail. Administrators only.

put.summary: Renames the library a received share is shown as here. Administrators only.

get.summary: What happened in the P2P network, newest first: pairings, connections, streams, refusals and revocations. Administrators only.

post.summary: Pairs the calling device with the user of a device invitation. Only through the P2P network.
Accepts a share invitation for the calling server. Only through the P2P network, server to server.

get.summary: Server to server: this server's name, the share's rules and libraries.
Server to server: the shared files, described (tags, content hash, artwork), 500 at a time.
Server to server: a shared file's audio, under the share's rules (conversion, bit-rate cap, downloads).

head.summary: Server to server: a shared file's audio, under the share's rules (conversion, bit-rate cap, downloads).

get.summary: Which online services are on (MusicBrainz, AcoustID, Cover Art Archive, LRCLib) and what each has done. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

put.summary: Turns online services on or off. They send only fingerprints, identifiers and artist, album and track names. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.
Uses your own AcoustID application key instead of the project's; null or empty goes back to the project's. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

get.summary: Performers and album artists with music the user can play, by name; optionally only those with music in a library. Pages of `first` items (default 50, at most 500) after the `after` cursor.

Albums with music the user can play, by title (or `sort`: `RECENTLY_ADDED` first, or `RANDOM`, the same order all day for the user and `seed`); optionally only those of an artist, or with music in a library.

Tracks the user can play, by title; optionally only those with a copy in a library. With albumId, all of the album's tracks in disc and track order, without paging. With `changedSince` (an earlier page's `serverTime`), only the tracks the catalog changed after it (tags, copies) or the user rated or played after it; the ones that left are found with trackIds.
The ids of every track the user can play (optionally of one library), at once and sorted: what a client compares with its own to see which tracks left the server.

post.summary: Applies the same tag changes to several tracks (at most 1000), as editTrack does. Returns them as they are now, in the order asked. Requires EDIT_METADATA.

Deletes tracks (at most 1000), or only their copies in `libraryId`: their files go to the trash of their locations (purged after 30 days) and they leave the catalog with their ratings, plays and playlist entries. One outcome per track. Requires DELETE_TRACKS.
Finds the server's tracks for an app's own (at most 1000 per call): by audio hash, MusicBrainz recording, AcoustID, and last by title, artist and album.

get.summary: A track with everything a properties dialog shows: its tags, its copies (library, path, size, format, quality, hash, dates), the user's rating and plays, and the analysis (tempo, key, loudness) when done.

patch.summary: Changes a track's tags: fields left out stay, empty ones ("", [], 0, the nil UUID) are cleared. Written to every copy's file (the original goes to the trash) and read back into the catalog. Returns the track as it is now: its id changes only when the new tags make it the same song as another track of its album, which it joins. Requires EDIT_METADATA and libraries the user adds to; read_only where the server cannot write, cue_sheet_track for tracks of a file split by a cue sheet, tags_unsupported for formats without tags, busy while a scan keeps the library.

delete.summary: Deletes a track (or only its copies in `libraryId`) as deleteTracks does. Requires DELETE_TRACKS.

put.summary: Makes the image (the request body: JPEG or PNG, other formats are converted to JPEG; at most 20 MB) the track's cover: embedded in its files as the front cover, replacing their pictures. An album without a cover takes it too. Requires EDIT_METADATA.

delete.summary: Removes the pictures of the track's files and its own image; it shows its album's cover, if the album has one. Requires EDIT_METADATA.

put.summary: Makes the image (the request body, as for setTrackArtwork) the album's cover, embedded in every file of its tracks. Requires EDIT_METADATA.

delete.summary: Removes the album's cover and the pictures of every file of its tracks (a cover image in its folder may bring it back at the next full scan). Requires EDIT_METADATA.

get.summary: A track's lyrics, with synchronized lines when known. not_found when it has none.
Overview of a track's audio for seek bars, from its best copy or the given file. not_found until the copy is analyzed.
The music videos in libraries the user can access, by title, with optional filters. Each says whether it plays with its song's audio and how to play it.
A music video, with the stretches where its audio and its song's line up (segments).

delete.summary: Moves a music video's file to the trash of its location and removes it from the catalog. Requires DELETE_TRACKS.

put.summary: Links a music video to a track's song (or, with no trackId, leaves it with no song); scans keep what a person chose. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES or EDIT_METADATA.

post.summary: Gives a music video back to automatic linking and live detection. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES or EDIT_METADATA.

put.summary: Marks a music video as a live performance or not. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES or EDIT_METADATA.

post.summary: Forgets a music video's alignment and aligns it again first of all. Requires MANAGE_LIBRARIES or EDIT_METADATA.

get.summary: How the server handles music videos. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

put.summary: Sets how the server handles music videos. Requires MANAGE_SETTINGS.

get.summary: A music video as MP4. Authenticate with a Bearer token or the `st` parameter of its stream URLs. `audio` is TRACK (the song's audio from the library where the video plays it, the video's own elsewhere) or VIDEO (its own); without it, the user's choice (myVideoSettings). Both have the same timeline: switch keeping the position. `rendition` (native, 2160p…360p) or `maxHeight`/`maxBitRate` choose the version. A version not made yet streams while it is made, without ranges (start later with `t`, in seconds); once made, it is served with ranges. X-Arcanist-Video-Audio says whose audio it has (VIDEO until the alignment is ready).

head.summary: A music video as MP4. Authenticate with a Bearer token or the `st` parameter of its stream URLs. `audio` is TRACK (the song's audio from the library where the video plays it, the video's own elsewhere) or VIDEO (its own); without it, the user's choice (myVideoSettings). Both have the same timeline: switch keeping the position. `rendition` (native, 2160p…360p) or `maxHeight`/`maxBitRate` choose the version. A version not made yet streams while it is made, without ranges (start later with `t`, in seconds); once made, it is served with ranges. X-Arcanist-Video-Audio says whose audio it has (VIDEO until the alignment is ready).

id.description: What Task<AdminPageResult> IExtensionAdminPage.RunAsync(AdminPageContext context, string action, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, JsonElement> values, CancellationToken cancellationToken) receives.

confirm.description: A question the panel asks before running it; null runs it at once.

key.description: A field's key, the one its value is saved under.

label.description: The label of a field, status, progress or list.

value.description: A field's current value, as JSON.

placeholder.description: What an empty text field shows.

min.description: The smallest number a field takes.

max.description: The largest number a field takes.

readOnly.description: A field shown but not edited.

text.description: The value of a status, the paragraph of a notice, or a progress's line.

tone.description: The color of a status or notice.

percent.description: How far a progress went, from 0 to 100.

AdminBlock.description: A piece of a section, built with its Field, Status, Notice, Progress and List methods.

refreshSeconds.description: Read the page again this often while it is open (to follow a progress); null never.

oneOf.description: What the extension still needs before it works (tools to download, an account to set…), or null when nothing: the panel offers it right after the extension starts, and at the top of the page, with the administrator's consent.

message.description: What happened, for a notice in the panel.

errors.description: Problems by field key, in the extension's words.

AdminPageResult.description: How saving or an action went.

actions.description: Buttons at the end of the section.

description.description: Why it is needed and what it does (downloads, from where, how big).

items.description: What will be installed or done, one line each.

action.description: The page's action that does it (Task<AdminPageResult> IExtensionAdminPage.RunAsync(AdminPageContext context, string action, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, JsonElement> values, CancellationToken cancellationToken)).

AdminSetup.description: Something an extension needs before it works, run with the administrator's consent.

AdminTone.description: The color a status or notice is shown in.
